A New Keynesian/DSGE read of the June 16, 2021 FOMC statement remains clearly accommodative: policy rates held at 0–0.25% under average inflation targeting, ongoing Treasury/MBS purchases ($80B/$40B per month), and floor-system tools (IOER 0.15%, ON RRP 0.05%) to preserve easy financial conditions while looking through transitory inflation.

Beige Book signals reinforce a moderately positive macro backdrop with frictions: across Districts, economic activity and employment are rising, with consumer and business spending contributing to growth; manufacturing production is expanding; residential real estate is strong amid tight inventories; financial conditions are supportive. At the same time, firms report labor availability constraints and wage pressures, broad price increases tied to supply bottlenecks, and more cautious sentiment in commercial real estate and construction. These corroborate the FOMC’s accommodative stance while highlighting near-term constraints and inflation pressures.

SLOOS nuances the transmission: banks eased for residential real estate, HELOCs, and several consumer categories and for IG C&I, but standards remain tighter than pre‑pandemic for many consumers; some tightening persists for nonprime auto and below‑IG borrowers; CRE underwriting remains cautious. Netting Beige Book strength with uneven credit supply keeps the outlook constructive but balanced rather than exuberant.
